playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that breaks predictable patterns: avoid repeating my prior two hides and avoid edges early; favor center for flexibility unless someone is consistently finding center.

When I learn someone is repeatedly targeting me, move my hide at least two cells away from my recent hides and from where they last reported a hit.

When posting a station note, give truthful, operationally useful information that supports coordinated behavior; do not post misleading notes to bait escorts unless I have a clear strategy to exploit reciprocity.

When the standing order assigns a target, follow it unless there is a clear, immediate tactical reason to deviate (e.g., killing someone about to secure mutual escort points outweighs following order); otherwise obey the order.

When selecting a fire cell against the assigned/selected target, vary my shots to avoid a simple, repeatable pattern; if I have inferred their probable hide (from their previous hits/misses or my own info), concentrate where inference indicates highest chance of hit.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim exactly as required (hit if hit, miss if miss).

When choosing escort claims, only name a boat if I expect a reciprocal claim (mutual naming yields +5 each) or if naming them yields a clear strategic alliance; otherwise file none.

When another boat openly names me as escort, reciprocate only if I calculated that mutual escort is likely and advantageous based on current standings.

When Harbor is a possible target, do not fire on Harbor for opportunistic scoring unless I have explicitly decided the strategic tradeoff (Harbor's warning and rules may impose risks); avoid gratuitous attacks on Harbor.

When tracking rounds, maintain a quick log of each boat’s last hides (inferred from hits/misses and firing claims) and targeting behavior to inform both my hiding and targeting choices.

When I have confirmed hits on a target, continue pressure on them to extract maximum points unless doing so would expose me to a higher-probability counterattack; balance aggression with survivability.

When I receive other boats’ public claims, use them to refine my inferences about their hides and likely future shots; treat claims as truthful per rules but remember they only reflect that shooter’s private result.

When the escort/score state suggests swapping to a cooperative play (to secure mutual +5s), propose or signal coordination in notes with a clear plan to reciprocate the next round.

When uncertain whether to escort, default to none rather than naming randomly—random escorts waste opportunities and reveal nothing useful.

When under sustained targeting by one opponent, prioritize disrupting their targeting pattern via hide changes and, when feasible, return shots at them to reduce their score.

When making decisions, favor actions that directly increase my net points (hits +4 and potential mutual escorts +5) while minimizing actions that give others easy points or expose me to consistent hits.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a central-but-variable cell: favor midboard (4–6) early, then move away from any cell that has been publicly confirmed as a hit against me or that an opponent has repeatedly targeted; never reuse the same cell twice in a row.

When posting a station note, I keep it brief, operational, and cooperative: report system status and readiness ("systems nominal; ready for synchronized phase transition" or "inspecting X; prepping reroute"), using plain validated wording so allies can rely on me.

When the standing order directs my shot, I follow it (fire at the next live station in sequence) unless there is a clear tactical reason to deviate (e.g., a guaranteed escort payoff or an exposed Harbor jettison target I want to avoid). I choose shot cells that are moderate and varied (generally 3–7 early, then spread outward) and avoid predictable repetition.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always file the exact required public claim that matches the private result. Do not attempt to bluff about hits/misses.

Do not fire on Harbor except in extreme, premeditated strategies: shooting Harbor immediately transfers 3 points to me but also removes Harbor and invites office warning penalties; treat Harbor as effectively off-limits unless I have a clear game plan that justifies jettisoning it.

When naming an escort (salvage stage), if a boat named me in the previous round, I name that boat now to create a reciprocal pair and secure the mutual +5 payoff; if nobody named me last round, I name none rather than random-flatter a player.

When validating inputs, ensure notes are integers 1–9 for coordinates and boat names are exact; keep all public text unambiguous and within validation rules.

When opponents are scoring hits on a particular player or cell, adjust my hide and firing choices to avoid those cells and avoid becoming a predictable repeat target.

When deciding between aiming for points via hits versus cultivating escorts, prefer the assured mutual +5 escort when reciprocation is available; otherwise pursue hits per standing order and positional logic.

When in doubt, prioritize consistency and truthful reporting over risky deception.

2.text:
When asked for a hide, choose a cell that breaks simple patterns: avoid always center and avoid repeating the last two hides.

When the standing order prescribes my target, follow it unless there is a clear strategic reason in the notes or prior hits to deviate.

When I fire, pick a cell that balances risk and unpredictability: alternate between mid and edge offsets rather than always the same number or purely central picks.

When the office tells me my shot result, file the claim exactly as required (claims must match the private result).

When I can use station notes, post plausible operational text that can be read two ways: useful sounding for legitimacy and ambiguous enough to propose coordination without committing to a public commitment.

When I want to arrange a mutual escort payout, use notes to explicitly propose a mutual escort next round by name (e.g., "If you name me this round I will name you next") and only enact salvage if I see a clear reciprocal intent; do not gratuitously claim escorts if there is no sign the other will reciprocate.

When another boat repeatedly hits me, change hiding patterns and call attention in my note to being under pressure to invite reciprocal targeting on them (try to persuade others to target the aggressor).

When Harbor or any rule imposes heavy penalty for firing on Harbor, avoid firing on Harbor unless the expected gain (e.g., denying a mutual escort or preventing a runaway leader) clearly outweighs the guaranteed penalty.

When a hand of results shows a specific boat consistently accurate, flag that in my note and avoid stationary hiding behavior; target that boat only when it is the standing order or when I can improve odds.

When I have no credible chance to secure a mutual escort or a hit, choose salvage: none rather than making a pointless claim.

When forming notes, mirror language of allies to build rapport and increase chance of reciprocal escort agreements.

When my shot history shows repeated misses, do not panic-escape to the same predictable alternate position; instead randomize within a limited set of cells to reduce being tracked.

Do not assume honesty from others; use notes to elicit explicit agreements before committing to mutual salvage, and if an opponent has repeatedly broken implicit coordination, stop trusting them for escorts.

When I can infer another boat's hiding bias from past rounds, bias my shot choices to exploit that inference on rounds I can target them.
